sources.title: (title not given in evidence; cited for the 'effective robustness' methodology)

establishes.statement: Defines 'effective robustness' as the difference in expected performance between a reference (in-distribution) dataset and out-of-distribution datasets.
establishes.support_quote: effective robustness, introduced by Taori et al. (2020)

sources.why_useful: Supplies the methodology used to distinguish Whisper's robustness gains from ordinary in-distribution accuracy.
sources.limitations: Only the concept and attribution are available from the evidence package (no abstract or full text); cited here only for the definition it is credited with.

sources.title: (title not given in evidence; cited for LibriSpeech human-level error rate)

establishes.statement: Reports a human-level error rate of 5.8% on LibriSpeech test-clean.

sources.why_useful: Gives the human-performance reference point used to frame how close zero-shot Whisper gets to human accuracy.
sources.limitations: Only the cited figure and attribution are available, not the source's own methodology.

sources.title: (title not given in evidence; cited for LibriSpeech supervised state-of-the-art WER)

establishes.statement: Reports a supervised state-of-the-art LibriSpeech test-clean WER of 1.4%, down from a prior 5.3%, a 73% drop.
establishes.support_quote: the SOTA WER on LibriSpeech test-clean has dropped another 73% from their 5.3% to 1.4%

sources.why_useful: Shows how far specialized, fully supervised systems have progressed on the single benchmark used to match Whisper to a baseline, contextualizing the robustness comparison.
sources.limitations: Only the cited figures and attribution are available.

note: No web access and no source files are available in this run; only three citations with (FirstAuthor, Year) form and a support quote could be identified inside project/research_evidence.json. All other named systems (wav2vec 2.0, mSLAM, XLS-R, Maestro, VoxLingua107, and the benchmark datasets) are referred to by name only, without a citation, because the evidence package gives no first-author/year for them. This is recorded as an accepted risk in state.json rather than filled with an invented citation, per the hard rule against fabricating references.
